name: Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts
description: This glass-vaulted landmark on Broad Street anchors Philadelphia's Avenue of the Arts and houses the acoustically celebrated 2,500-seat Marian Anderson Hall (formerly Verizon Hall). Beyond orchestral concerts, its stages host jazz, Broadway tours, dance and family programming throughout the year.

name: Academy of Music
highlight: The nation's oldest continuously operating opera house
description: Opened in 1857, this opulent, chandelier-lit hall is a National Historic Landmark and the resident home of Opera Philadelphia and the Philadelphia Ballet. Its gilded, horseshoe-shaped auditorium delivers grand productions and touring Broadway shows in a genuinely historic setting.

name: The Met Philadelphia
highlight: Restored 1908 opera house turned concert palace
description: Originally built as an opera house in 1908, this North Broad landmark reopened in 2018 after a lavish restoration and now packs its ornate 3,400-capacity hall with major touring artists. It draws big-name pop, rock, R&B and comedy acts to a room that blends grandeur with modern production.

name: The Mann Center
description: Set amid the greenery of Fairmount Park with sweeping views of the skyline, the Mann is Philadelphia's signature warm-weather venue for open-air concerts. Its covered pavilion and sprawling lawn host everything from the Philadelphia Orchestra's summer series to marquee touring headliners.

name: Franklin Music Hall
highlight: Historic 2,500-capacity room, the former Electric Factory
description: This cavernous former factory, long known as the Electric Factory, is one of the city's largest general-admission rooms and a magnet for national touring acts. Standing-room floor space and a balcony bar give it a raw, high-energy concert atmosphere.

name: Union Transfer
highlight: One of the city's best-sounding indie rooms
description: Housed in a former train depot, Union Transfer is beloved for its excellent acoustics, sliding stage and multiple bars that scale to any crowd size. It's a go-to stop for indie, rock and rising national artists, consistently ranked among Philadelphia's top mid-sized venues.

name: World Cafe Live
highlight: Intimate concerts and home of WXPN radio
description: Connected to public radio station WXPN, this two-stage venue pairs an upstairs listening room with a larger downstairs hall offering full food and drink service. Its refined, intimate setting makes it a favorite for singer-songwriters, jazz and roots artists.

name: The Fillmore Philadelphia
highlight: Converted Fishtown factory with a chandelier-lit hall
description: A restored industrial building in trendy Fishtown, the Fillmore hosts rising and established acts in its spacious main hall and the smaller upstairs Foundry room. Its vintage decor, big-name bookings and multiple bars make it a cornerstone of the neighborhood's nightlife.

name: Walnut Street Theatre
description: Founded in 1808, the Walnut is the oldest continuously operating theatre in the English-speaking world and the most subscribed theatre company in the nation. It stages a popular season of Broadway-style musicals, comedies and dramas in its intimate main auditorium.

name: Wilma Theater
highlight: Bold, contemporary and internationally minded productions
description: A Tony Award-winning company on the Avenue of the Arts, the Wilma is known for adventurous, boundary-pushing contemporary theater and its resident acting ensemble. Its modern 300-seat space offers an intimate vantage on ambitious new work and reimagined classics.

name: Xfinity Mobile Arena
highlight: The city's largest arena, formerly the Wells Fargo Center
description: Renamed the Xfinity Mobile Arena in 2025, this 21,000-seat venue in the South Philadelphia sports complex is home to the 76ers and Flyers. It also hosts the region's biggest arena concerts and touring spectacles year-round.

name: Johnny Brenda's
highlight: Beloved intimate Fishtown club with a horseshoe balcony
description: A cornerstone of Fishtown's music scene, Johnny Brenda's pairs a well-regarded gastropub downstairs with an intimate upstairs concert room ringed by a horseshoe balcony. Its sharp booking of indie and emerging acts makes it one of the city's most cherished small venues.
